input: SC-WOW-FALL-001 — the guardian's fall (SC-AEP-001 candidate). Sargeras, Zovaal, Neltharion, Arthas and Malygos each foresee a threat, override others' consent to stop it, take up a tool of control and become the threat. Repair is a voluntary successor: Bolvar, Pelagos, Kalecgos, Ebyssian, Illidan. Saul (1 Sam 13:12).

claims.text: The repair is a voluntary successor with a different method: Bolvar ('There must always be a Lich King', 3.3), Pelagos who volunteered to be the Arbiter (9.2), Kalecgos after Malygos, Ebyssian after Neltharion (10.1), Illidan as Sargeras's jailer by choice (7.3). Consent is what changes between the fallen guardian and the successor.

v2_extensions.source_text:
# SC-WOW-FALL-001: the guardian's fall, a recurring composite among Warcraft's antagonists

Read under SC-AEP-001. The bundle has five attributes: (1) a guardian's charge, (2) a foreseen threat, (3) a decision that the threat justifies overriding others' consent, (4) a tool of control taken up, (5) the guardian becomes the threat or its servant. A row counts as a CANDIDATE with at least three attributes, one of them relational (3 or 4), and one recorded difference.

## Instances
| Figure | Charge | Foreseen threat | Override | Tool | Outcome | Attributes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sargeras | champion of the Pantheon | the Void lords' plan to corrupt world-souls | burn all creation to deny the Void | the Burning Legion | imprisoned at the Seat of the Pantheon (7.3) | 5/5 (NOVEL for the motive: Chronicle Vol. 1) |
| Zovaal | the first Arbiter | an unseen power that the forces of Death were not ready for | remake reality; Domination | sigils, the Helm and Frostmourne | killed (9.2) | 5/5 |
| Neltharion | Earth-Warder | the Primalists' war | bind the dracthyr; take the Old Gods' power to win | the Oathbinder; the whispers | Deathwing; killed (4.3); essence recovered (10.1) | 5/5 (NOVEL for the first submission) |
| Arthas | prince and paladin | the plague's spread | purge Stratholme; take up Frostmourne | Frostmourne | the Lich King; killed (3.3) | 5/5 |
| Malygos | Aspect of Magic | mortal magic drawing the Legion | war on mortal spellcasters (the Nexus War) | the ley lines | killed (3.0) | 5/5 |
| Xe'ra | naaru of the Army of the Light | the Legion | bind Illidan to the Light's prophecy | the Light | destroyed by Illidan (7.3) | 3/5 PARTIAL: she does not become the threat |
| The Lightblinded Vanguard | paragons of the Light | (not stated) | zealotry: smite all who oppose | the Light | killed (Voidspire, 12.0) | 3/5 PARTIAL: no foreseen threat in the text |
| Iridikron | (none: he refused the gift) | the titans' 'stain' | sells the Dark Heart to the Void | the Dark Heart | alive (10.2) | EXCLUDED: no guardian's charge |
| Xal'atath | harbinger of Dimensius | (unrevealed) | (unrevealed) | the Dark Heart | final boss of 12.2 (ANNOUNCED) | EXCLUDED until her motive is shown |

Outside Warcraft, the same bundle appears in Anakin's turn to save Padme (SC-VESSEL-SW-001) and Daenerys's slide (SC-GOT-001). Each is a candidate, not proof of influence.

## The repair: a voluntary successor
Each fallen guardian is followed by one who takes the charge by choice and with a different method: Kalecgos after Malygos (chosen by his flight, he shares magic rather than hoarding it); Bolvar after Arthas ("There must always be a Lich King", 3.3); Pelagos, who volunteered to become the Arbiter after Zovaal (9.2); Ebyssian after Neltharion, chosen by his brothers (10.1); Illidan, who chose to stay as Sargeras's jailer (7.3). The successor's consent is the repair.

## Tradition (candidates)
- Saul: "Because I saw that the people were scattered from me ... I forced myself therefore, and offered a burnt offering" (1 Sam 13:11-12). A king who overrides the rule from fear of the coming threat and loses the kingdom (13:13-14). Attributes 1, 2, 3, 5. CANDIDATE. Successor: David, who refuses to seize power from Saul (1 Sam 24:6).
- Caiaphas: "it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not" (John 11:47-50), from fear the Romans would take the nation (11:48). Attributes 1, 2, 3. CANDIDATE.
- Peter: rebukes the cross to protect his teacher and is told "Get thee behind me, Satan" (Matt 16:21-23); later draws a sword and is told to put it away (John 18:10-11). The protective override refused. CONTRAST.
- The covering cherub: "Thou art the anointed cherub that covereth ... till iniquity was found in thee" (Ezek 28:14-15); with Isa 14:12-15. A guardian's fall. Reading these as Satan's fall is interpretive tradition, not the text's plain subject (the prince of Tyre; the king of Babylon). CANDIDATE with that difference recorded.
- The pattern's difference from Lucifer in tradition: the tradition's fall is pride (1 Tim 3:6); the Warcraft bundle's fall is fear. Recorded, not resolved.


---

## Verbatim t594u source (Shax)

Now you can go ahead and map out all the invariants and classes of World of Warcraft and bosses throughout theology. I even go far as dragonflight as being when the dragon gets to spread their wings for good or and defeat the bad dragon, you know, the good Tok'ra versus the bad ghouls. All that good stuff.

outputs.literal_translation:
Speaker [Shax/Curtis Kingsley] (t594u) asks for the invariants and bosses of World of Warcraft through theology.
Canon check: five guardians fall by fear-driven override; each is followed by a voluntary successor.
Residuals: fear, not pride.
outputs.public_translation: Many of Warcraft's great villains started as protectors who saw a danger coming, decided it justified taking away other people's choices, and became the danger. The fix each time is someone who takes up the same job by choice and does it differently. None of this is a claim about the real world.

Xal'atath's motive is not revealed; 12.2 Eclipse is ANNOUNCED. Reading Ezek 28 and Isa 14 as Satan's fall is interpretive tradition. Secondary source: Warcraft Wiki citing the game and novels.
